entries.german:
1318. 26. September. Hohenfurt. — Peter von Rosenberg schenkt zum Seelen heile seiner Gemahlin Viola dem Stifte Hohenfurt die Dörfer Eibenstein, Stiftung, Schwarzenbach, Frauenthal und „zu den höfen".

In nomine sanete et indiuidue trinitatis amen. Quoniam humane condicio nature secundum status sui qualitatem mobiliter discurren» 67 prouiorque ad malum quam ad Immun. ad instabile quam ad stabile fore dinoscitur euidenter, necesse est, gesta hominum, ne in obluio- nis materiam decidant, apicibus seripturarum sagaciter perhennari. Eapropter nos Petrus de Rosenberch summus regni Boemie camera- rius vniuersis tam presentibus quam futuris hanc litteram inspecturis. in noticiam deducimus clariorem, quod ob remedium anime felicis recordacionis domine Wpole vxoris nostre dulcissime monasterio beate virginis Marie in Altovado ordinis Cysterciensis nostre funda- cionis villas nostras Eybenstein, Styphtung, Swarczenpach, Freu- dental et curias, que wlgariter „dacz den hoefen" nuncupantur, cum omnibus pertinenciis earundem, agris cultis incultis pratis suluis pascuis aquis piscacionibus molendinis aquaruinve decursibus et montibus , ea metarum, qua prefatas habuimus villas, certa et con- sveta distinccione pleno iure, quo nus antecessoresque nostri incon- cusse ipsas possedimus, iusto donauimus proprietatis tytulo perpetuo possidendas, excepto dumtaxat iure nostro feodali, quo nobiles illius districti ab antiquo progenitoribus nostris et nobis sunt astricti, quod nobis et nostris successoribus perpetuo reseruamus. Ne igitur prenominate fundacioni nostre dilecte, cuius promocionis vtilitas singularitcr nostro cordi insidet, de nostra sibi in pretaxatis villis facta donacione alicuius litis sev controuersie calumpnia possit in futurum suboriri, presentem sibi tradidimus litteram sigilli nostri maioris robore consignatam. Datum in Altovado anno domini mille- simo treceutesimo decimo octauo in vigilia sanctorum martirum Cosme et Damyani. Ein etwas beschädigtes, ziemlich grosses, an Pergamentstreifen hängendes Siegel in weissem Wachs. — Ein Kitter hoch zu Rosse, dessen Schabracke mit Rosen besäet ist, schwingt mit der Rechten ein Schwert und hält in der Linken einen Schild mit der fünfblätterigen Rose; die Zierde des Helmes besteht ¡n eben solchen zwei Rosen. — -j- Sigillvm. Domi ri. De. Rosen- berc. . . .
entries.english:
In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, amen. Since human nature, according to its condition, is evidently changeable in its course, more inclined to evil than to good, and to what is unstable than to what is stable, it is necessary to preserve human deeds carefully in written records, lest they fall into oblivion. Therefore we, Peter von Rosenberg, chief chamberlain of the Kingdom of Bohemia, make known to all present and future who see this letter that, for the salvation of the soul of our dearly beloved wife, Lady Viola of blessed memory, we have donated, with rightful title of ownership, to the monastery of the Blessed Virgin Mary at Hohenfurt of the Cistercian Order, founded by us, our villages Eibenstein, Stiftung, Schwarzenbach, Frauenthal, and the estates commonly called “zu den Höfen,” with all their appurtenances: cultivated and uncultivated fields, meadows, woods, pastures, waters, fisheries, mills, watercourses, and mountains. We grant them with the same certain and customary boundaries by which we held these villages, with full ownership, as we and our predecessors possessed them without interruption, to be held in perpetuity, except only for our feudal right, by which the nobles of that district have been bound to our ancestors and to us from ancient times; that right we reserve perpetually for ourselves and our successors.

Lest any claim or dispute should arise in the future concerning our donation to this beloved foundation, whose advancement is especially dear to our heart, we have delivered this letter to it, authenticated by the strength of our great seal. Given at Hohenfurt in the year of the Lord 1318, on the eve of Saints Cosmas and Damian, martyrs.

Seal: A somewhat damaged, fairly large seal hangs from a parchment tag in white wax. It depicts a knight on horseback, his horse’s covering strewn with roses; he brandishes a sword in his right hand and holds a shield bearing a five-petaled rose in his left. The helmet ornament likewise consists of two such roses. Inscription: “Sigillvm. Domi ri. De. Rosenberc. . . .”
